brief:
REPAIR THE FEATURE ITEM S6 JUST SHIPPED. It is ON by default and it has a regression in it. Fix that before anything else.

Context: item S6 (commit d57170e9, issue 1201) made the netlister write a specialised copy of a cell by itself when an instance sets a property the symbol's `format=` never reads but the cell's own schematic body consumes. That is the user's own bug report -- they typed `modelp=pfet_01v8_lvt` on two bandgap passgates and XSCHEM threw it away. The feature works: 653 shipped decks byte-diffed unmoved, and the shipped bandgap sheet with its hand-typed `schematic=` tokens stripped now netlists x5/x6 to a low-Vt body with nothing typed on the sheet. But S6's own verify pass filed six defects INSIDE the new behaviour and shipped anyway. This item closes them.

The driver has ALREADY RULED on the question S6 asked: the feature STAYS ON. Do not gate it behind a setting, do not turn it off, do not re-ask. Fix the defects instead.

== MANDATORY, IN THIS ORDER ==

**1204 -- the regression, and the reason this item exists.** `xschem netlist -nohier` ("netlist current schematic only") emits `xt1 net2 advpass__modelp_pfet_01v8_lvt W_P=0.5` and defines that subcircuit nowhere -- not in that file, not in any other netlist file, not in any library. The simulator rejects the deck. Before 1201 the same line read `xt1 net2 advpass`, naming a real cell the user's other netlist files define, so this is a REGRESSION on a mode that used to work. Worse, the info window simultaneously tells the user in plain English that XSCHEM wrote the copy for them and they need do nothing. Cause, re-confirmed on the shipped source: `auto_spec_begin()` is called unconditionally at `src/spice_netlist.c:418`, ahead of `spice_netlist(fd, 0)`, while the `if(global)` block at `:477` is what actually writes the `.subckt` bodies -- so with global=0 the call lines get specialised names and no bodies follow. Decide deliberately between the two honest answers and say which you chose and why: (a) in single-sheet mode do not specialise at all, so the call line names the plain cell exactly as it did before 1201; or (b) write the specialised bodies in single-sheet mode too. Whichever you pick, the info-window sentence must match what actually happened -- a tool that says it wrote a copy it did not write is RULING D5-1, which is the whole reason this area exists. Check every other netlist backend for the same shape: spectre, vhdl, verilog, tedax.

**1202 -- silent loss of a setting the user typed.** `auto_spec_collides()` (`src/actions.c:4210`) asks four questions and never asks what `schematic=` names the OTHER copies on the sheet have typed. So a copy that hand-types the very name the netlister would have invented silently loses its own setting. That is the same defect class as issue 0982 and as the original 0970 -- a typed setting that does nothing, without a word -- which makes shipping it inside 0970's own fix particularly bad.

**1203 -- ambiguous cell naming.** The canonical key joins token/value pairs with a double underscore, so two DIFFERENT setting lists can spell ONE cell name. Two copies that should get two bodies quietly share one, and only the first one's settings survive. Pick an unambiguous encoding, prove the ambiguity is gone with a row that constructs the colliding pair, and keep the names readable to a person -- the user reads these names in the deck.

**1206 -- an empty setting value writes a second identical copy of a cell.** Wasteful and confusing; a copy that differs in nothing is not a copy.

== DO THESE TOO IF THIS PASS CAN DO THEM SAFELY; LEAVE THEM FILED AND SAY SO IF NOT ==

**1205** -- `src/token.c:3580` short-circuits past the very check the sentence below it asserts, so the netlist warning tells the user "the drawing does not use this setting" without having looked. A sentence asserting a fact it never established.

**1209** -- a specialised copy loses the symbol/schematic pin-mismatch highlight. A real check silently stops running on exactly the cells this feature creates.

**1208** -- test hygiene, cheap: rows AS6/AS26 of the new suite fingerprint a whole deck INCLUDING the absolute-path header written at `src/spice_netlist.c:332` and `:719`, so the suite passes only in this checkout.

== DO NOT TOUCH ==
**1207** is PRE-EXISTING and not caused by 1201: eight shipped `xschem_library/viewdraw_import/xschem_lib/dti_*` sheets segfault on netlist in every backend (signal 11) when the viewdraw symbols resolve. Real and worth fixing, but it is not this item's subject and it is a crash in old code. Leave it filed.

== EVIDENCE THE FIX MUST CARRY ==
* Re-run the S6 acceptance measurement: the shipped bandgap sheet with only its two hand-typed `schematic=passgate_lvtp` tokens stripped must still netlist x5/x6 to a low-Vt body while x3/x4/x7 keep the plain one.
* Re-run the FULL shipped-deck byte-diff (S6 measured 654 sheets, 646 netlisting cleanly, 8 being 1207's crashers). Zero unexplained movement, before and after this repair.
* `test_auto_specialize_1201` (44 checks today) grows a row per defect fixed, each written RED first and watched fail.
* `test_unused_attr_0970` is 67 and `test_op_annot` is 484 at d57170e9 -- neither may drop.
* T1 run SOLO, ZERO counted failures.

== ISSUE NUMBERS ==
Next free is **1210**. 1000-1199, 0500-0599 and 0700-0799 are RESERVED for other branches -- never use them.

== PLAIN ENGLISH IS A HARD REQUIREMENT ==
User ruling, verbatim: 'wording too cryptic. Give it in plain english with context, 9th grade level.' Every sentence that reaches a user's screen is written for a first-time user who says schematic, library, cell, file, setting. The user has also said this session, about a long answer: 'I still have no idea what is going on ... I want a few lines, not 2 pages to read.' Short and concrete beats thorough and unreadable.
